intervention.message: No nudge today (30 minutes logged). Meika will nudge you on days you log 60+ minutes, when your spending has tended to run higher.

factors.label: Tracking coverage
factors.detail: 60 day(s) tracked since 22 Jul 2026, 39 with logged screen time (2335 minutes in total). Days with nothing logged count as zero exposure.

factors.label: Screen time lines up with your spending
factors.detail: On days with more logged exposure, your discretionary spending that day and the next tends to be higher too (Spearman rho = 0.45, permutation p = 0.021 against 46 time-shifted comparisons, 59 days). Weekly rhythm was removed first, so busier weekends don't count. This is an association, not proof that one causes the other.

factors.label: After high-exposure days
factors.detail: On the 16 days with 60+ minutes logged, discretionary spending that day and the next averaged ₩55,597, vs ₩18,538 after the 21 days with none: ₩37,059 more. 60 minutes is the top third of your own exposed days (at least 30).

factors.label: Exploratory: which day the spending lands
factors.detail: Exposure vs discretionary spending the same day, one day and two days later (lag 0: rho 0.21, lag 1: rho 0.42, lag 2: rho 0.26). Not corrected for multiple comparisons, so read these as hints only.

factors.label: No nudge today
factors.detail: No nudge today (30 minutes logged). Meika will nudge you on days you log 60+ minutes, when your spending has tended to run higher.

limitations: Association, not causation. Mood, boredom, payday or a stressful week can drive both screen time and spending; weekly rhythm is removed, other rhythms are not.
Exposure is self-reported. Days with nothing logged are treated as zero exposure, so gaps in logging weaken any link Meika can find.
Meika has no access to social-media or app-usage data. Everything here comes from what you logged.
With a few weeks of data, permutation p-values are coarse: with n days, the smallest possible p is about 1/(n - 14).
Only the same-day-or-next-day test was fixed in advance. The per-lag and per-kind numbers are exploratory and not corrected for multiple comparisons.
Discretionary spending means cafes & dining, apparel and electronics, the same impulse-prone set the early-warning module uses.
